title: Traffic Slimming Release Canvas + Customer Comm Draft (May 2026)
body:
Purpose
This is a concise, pragmatic plan for a traffic-slimming release (aka targeted throughput reduction) to validate a runtime optimization landed in runtime PR#4821. Goal: exercise canary cohorts across regions while minimizing blast radius and giving account teams predictable behavior to communicate to customers.

TL;DR
- Start small (0.5% global) with aggressive telemetry gating.
- Apply regional bucket throttles for low-latency customers (EU, US-W) to preserve SLOs.
- Customer comms: pre-notify enterprise tier customers with opt-out window.
- Fallback policy: automatic rollback at signal X or manual rollback on human-approved threshold.

High-level rollout calendar (working draft)
- Day -3 (2026-05-08): Final smoke in staging, synthesis run for 1M tokens. Notify SRE & CS on intent.
- Day -1 (2026-05-10): Canary build promoted to canary slot, internal canary testing window (4h).
- Day 0 (2026-05-11): 0.5% global traffic, regional buckets: US-West 0.2%, US-East 0.15%, EU 0.1%, APAC 0.05%. Run 6h.
- Day 1 (2026-05-12): If green, increase to 2% global (same regional proportions). Run 12h.
- Day 2 (2026-05-13): 5% global. Run 24h.
- Day 4 (2026-05-15): 10% global; begin ramp to 25% over next 48h if stable.
- Emergency window: any time — rollback to previous model variant and remove throttles.

Pre-launch checklist (quick, must-pass items)
- [ ] Final PR merged & tagged: runtime PR#4821 (confirm checksum).
- [ ] Canary image built and pushed to registry (image: runtime:v4821-canary).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards: tokens/s, p50/p95 latency, error-rate, OOMs instrumented. Links in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Alert runbook updated for new metric names (see alert IDs below).
- [ ] Customer communications ready: CS draft, legal review for enterprise notices.
- [ ] Throttle rules codified in traffic-router config (store revision id + reviewer).
- [ ] Rollback owner assigned for 24h (primary + backup).

Throttle curve & cohort allocation (textual)
- Rationale: small, regionally skewed starts to limit impact on latency-sensitive regions. Adjust by observed p95 latency delta.
- Numeric plan (example):
  - 0–6h: 0.5% global (US-W 0.2, US-E 0.15, EU 0.1, APAC 0.05)
  - 6–18h: 2% global (same regional fractions)
  - 18–42h: 5% global
  - 42–96h: 10% -> 25% (progressive step-ups every 12h subject to gates)

Monitoring signals & hard gates
- Primary signals (automated gates):
  - p95 latency delta > +250ms sustained for 10m => fail gate => auto-decrease to previous step.
  - error-rate increase > 1.0% absolute over baseline for 5m => fail gate.
  - OOM count > 2 per 1h across canary nodes => fail gate.
- Secondary signals (operator review):
  - Small but steady increase in tail latency (p99) or token cost deviation > 12% => needs human review.
  - CS tickets from enterprise accounts describing throttling/slow responses (>= 3 in 24h) => escalate.

Automated rollback policy
- Auto-rollback if any primary gate trips during the hold window. Rollback sequence: (1) route new cohorts back to previous stable variant using routing-policy vX-previous; (2) scale down canary nodes; (3) notify #release-ops and page SRE on-call.
- Manual rollback: owner + oncall must acknowledge and execute; document reason in ticket RE-1192.

Customer communications (templates & timing)
- Pre-notice (to enterprise customers, T-48h): short note explaining a small test to improve throughput & reliability. Provide opt-out link and support SLA.
  "Hello — on 2026-05-11 we will run a brief, staged test of a runtime optimization that reduces cost for certain workloads. We expect no customer-visible impact; if you prefer to be excluded from the test, reply to this email or open ticket RE-1192-optout. — Maya (Release Ops)"
- If gated failure or rollback occurs: "We detected anomalous latency for a small percentage of requests and rolled back the update. No customer data was impacted. We're investigating and will follow up with a root cause within 48h."
- Post-release note (final): bullet summary of changes, measurable outcomes (tokens/sec improvement, p95 reduction), list of affected cohorts, link to follow-up RCA.

Draft release notes (short)
- Title: runtime: inference kernel selection refinements (v4821)
- Summary: Improved kernel selection for medium-length sequences resulting in lower per-token CPU and marginally improved p95 latency for cached workloads.
- Known limitations: small cohort-specific warmup penalty under very short-request distributions (we saw transient p95 blips in US-West during load tests).

Observability and dashboards (links)
- Canary dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency (split by region & model_variant), error codes, token rate, node mem headroom.
- Cost dashboard: token-unit cost delta vs baseline.
- Quick links: GH PR, staging run logs, synthetic-run CSVs (attached in Confluence).

Roles & responsibilities during rollout
- Release lead: Maya Chen (primary) — overall go/no-go, customer comms.
- Rollback owner: Omar Singh (primary), Priya Kapoor (backup).
- Observability lead: Samir Patel — monitors dashboards and triggers alerts.
- CS contact: Elena Morris — handles enterprise opt-outs and replies.

Post-release retro prompts (to fill after release)
- What telemetry would we add to make the gate earlier/more precise?
- Was the regional split effective? Did any region show systematic instability?
- Did customer comms prevent surprises for enterprise customers?
- Cost vs latency trade-off: did we meet predicted unit-cost improvements?

Open questions / TODOs
- [ ] Finalize opt-out flow: email vs support portal ticket. (Priya)
- [ ] Confirm routing-policy rollback script and test it in staging. (Omar)
- [ ] Add synthetic workload that mimics shortest-request tail (to catch warmup p95 blips). (Samir)
- [ ] Legal review of enterprise notice language (Elena).

Notes to self / informal bits
- If p95 blips appear only at ramp start and settle within 30m, consider keeping pace but tighten next gate.
- Keep an eye on token cost delta — sometimes micro-ops reduce CPU but increase memory thrash.
- Slack shorthand: tag & start thread in #release-ops with prefix [traffic-slim-4821].

Appendix: Signals & alert IDs (for runbook updates)
- ALERT:RE_CANARY_LATENCY_SPIKE (p95_delta_10m > 250ms)
- ALERT:RE_CANARY_ERROR_RATE (absolute_error_rate_5m > 1.0%)
- ALERT:RE_CANARY_OOM (oom_count_1h > 2)

---
Small, pragmatic, focused on minimizing surprise. This doc will become the short-run runbook that sits next to the longer confluence page. Use this as the coordination canvas for shift leads and CS reps.

Comments / revisions log (short)
- 2026-05-03: Draft created (Maya)
- 2026-05-06: Added region allocations and gate numbers after staging sims (Samir)
- 2026-05-09: Customer comms drafted, awaiting legal (Elena)

(End)
